# 094 · A participant node that sends its vote before logging it restarts as if it had not voted

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✗ Violation: EveryStepIsOneOfTheModel, 2-step trace (the recorded runs)** | functional | critical | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`ParticipantNode#act`](../../examples/apps/quorum/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/quorum/twopc/ParticipantNode.java) | [D1: Protocol model checking](../../examples/apps/quorum/spec/README.md) |

> The participant node logs its new state before it sends its vote, so that a crash between the two loses the vote and not the state, and a restart that reads `PREPARED` holds the locks. A developer swaps the two to get the vote to the coordinator sooner. The rule is untouched, every contract holds, and the model's six configurations are as green as before: the model says the participant logs first, and nothing in it checks that the node does. The recorded runs do. TLC walks the run in which a participant crashes after its first I/O operation and finds, at its second step, a state the model has no action for: the yes vote is on its way and the log still says working. A restart from that log aborts, and the vote can still reach the coordinator.

Tags: [distributed-transactions](../README.md#tag-distributed-transactions), [crash-recovery](../README.md#tag-crash-recovery), [write-ahead-ordering](../README.md#tag-write-ahead-ordering), [tla-trace-validation](../README.md#tag-tla-trace-validation), [tla-fault-configuration](../README.md#tag-tla-fault-configuration), [generated-operator](../README.md#tag-generated-operator), [multiple-configurations](../README.md#tag-multiple-configurations)

## The change

In `ParticipantNode.act`, the loop that sends a transition's votes moves above the log write, with the comment that the coordinator is waiting, so send first and log after. The node test that pinned the order, in which a crash after the first I/O operation of a vote leaves the yes logged and unsent and the restart holds it, is replaced by one in which the same crash leaves the vote out, which is what the developer wanted to see. `Participant.decide` is untouched.

**Before** ([`ParticipantNode.java`](../../examples/apps/quorum/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/quorum/twopc/ParticipantNode.java), line 64):

```java
return switch (decision) {
    case Transition<ParticipantState, ParticipantEffect> t -> {
        state = t.next();
        log.write(state); // logged before the vote goes out: a crash from here on loses the vote only
        for (ParticipantEffect effect : t.effects()) {
            network.send(new VoteMessage(name, effect == ParticipantEffect.VOTE_YES ? Vote.YES : Vote.NO), faults);
        }
        yield true;
    }
    case Unchanged<ParticipantState, ParticipantEffect> u -> false;
```

**After:**

```java
return switch (decision) {
    case Transition<ParticipantState, ParticipantEffect> t -> {
        state = t.next();
        for (ParticipantEffect effect : t.effects()) { // the coordinator is waiting: send first, log after
            network.send(new VoteMessage(name, effect == ParticipantEffect.VOTE_YES ? Vote.YES : Vote.NO), faults);
        }
        log.write(state);
        yield true;
    }
    case Unchanged<ParticipantState, ParticipantEffect> u -> false;
```

| the recorded runs (`spec/TwoPhaseCommitTrace.cfg`) | the Java nodes against the model: the coordinator node, its log and its broadcast, and the participant nodes, their logs and their votes, run through eleven scripted scenarios with crashes of either process injected after a given I/O operation, the state after each step recorded in the model's variables (`TwoPhaseCommitTraces.tla`, regenerated from the patched classes); TLC walks each recorded run and checks that it starts in the model's initial state and that every step is a step of the model's next-state relation. A step the model has no action for is one the glue took that the model's verdicts do not cover | Participants = {"p1", "p2", "p3"}, MaxCrashes = 2, MaxParticipantCrashes = 2 | ✗ Violation: EveryStepIsOneOfTheModel, 2-step trace |

TLC found a run of the system under the recorded runs, 2 steps long, whose last step violates the action property **EveryStepIsOneOfTheModel** (every step the nodes recorded is a step of the model's next-state relation: an action of one part, or a step that changes nothing. A step the model has no action for is one the glue around the rules took, which the model's verdicts do not cover). Each step is the next state the implementation recorded:

1. **Start of the recorded run** `"a participant crashes after logging its yes and before sending it, and the timer aborts"`, the model's initial state as the nodes recorded it: `crashes = 0`, `decision = "NONE"`, `inbox = {}`, `pcrashes = 0`, `phase = "COLLECTING"`, `pstate = [p1 |-> "WORKING", p2 |-> "WORKING", p3 |-> "WORKING"]`, `pup = [p1 |-> TRUE, p2 |-> TRUE, p3 |-> TRUE]`, `up = TRUE`, `votes = [p1 |-> "NONE", p2 |-> "NONE", p3 |-> "NONE"]`
2. **TraceNext**, the next state the nodes recorded, after the step the comment in `TwoPhaseCommitTraces.tla` names. `inbox = {[from |-> "p1", vote |-> "YES"]}`, `pcrashes = 1`, `pup = [p1 |-> FALSE, p2 |-> TRUE, p3 |-> TRUE]`

TLC walked the recorded runs, one recorded state after the other, and held each step to the model's next-state relation `Next`: the check covers the scripted runs and no others, which is what the model's own configurations are for.

**What the verdict rests on.** TLC counted how often a step of the model took each row of the generated operators. A row no step takes is one the model says nothing about, whatever the verdict.

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

No: every existing unit test passes (`java -ea net.terminalvalue.quorum.Tests`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

High, and the kind a review lets through. Two statements swap places in a class that holds no logic, the rule and its contract are untouched, the tests pass, and the six configurations of the model report what they reported before, since the model checks the rules and takes the glue around them on trust: it says the participant logs before it sends, and nothing in it checks that. A reviewer who knows the write-ahead rule will stop here; one reading the comment will see a latency improvement.

## Why the verdict is right

The six configurations of the model report their previous counts, 728, 736, 3,448, 2,728, 12,754 and 18,636 states, since the rules the model's operators are generated from have not changed. The seventh, `TwoPhaseCommitTrace.cfg`, regenerates the recorded runs from the patched nodes and holds them to the model. The scenario in which a participant crashes after its first I/O operation was written for the log write; with the vote sent first, the crash falls after the send, and the recorded state after that step has p1's yes vote in `inbox`, p1 down, and `pstate[p1]` still `WORKING`, read from the log. The model's `Vote` logs `PREPARED` and then sends, or crashes with the vote lost or not; no action of the model puts a vote out from a participant whose logged state is working, so the action property `EveryStepIsOneOfTheModel` fails at the second step of the eleventh run, and TLC prints the run's name with the state. What the run does next is the harm: the restart reads `WORKING` and aborts on the committed rule, which is correct for a participant that logged nothing because such a participant sent nothing, while the vote this one did send is still on its way to the coordinator. In the scripted run the coordinator's timer aborts before that vote is counted; with the vote delivered and the other two yes, the coordinator commits, which is example 093's outcome from a correct rule and the wrong order of two lines. The sixth configuration proved the rule safe on the strength of the order.

## What to do

Reject. The log write comes first for a participant as for the coordinator: the write-ahead rule is what the restart's reading of the log relies on, and the model's participant-crash configurations prove the rule correct on the strength of it. The recorded runs are regenerated from the patched classes on every build, so the next change to the node is held to the model the same way.

## Notes

- The two-phase-commit model (`apps/quorum/spec/TwoPhaseCommit.tla`) is built like Box Office's: the coordinator's state machine is generated from its B8 contract. An example of this model is checked under every configuration the model lists, and its verdict is the first that fails.
- Trace validation (`TwoPhaseCommitTrace.cfg`): the Java nodes run through scripted scenarios with crashes injected, the state after each step recorded in the model's variables, and TLC checks every recorded step against the model's next-state relation as an action property. It sees changes to the glue around the kernels that no contract and no other configuration sees.
- Two configurations let the participants crash, between steps or between logging a vote and sending it, and restart on the participant's rule, a third generated operator (`Participant#decide`).
- Caught by its recorded run, at the step where the vote is out and the log still says working.

## Evidence

How the verdict was reached: three participants: TLC 2.19 explored 728 distinct states to depth 11 in 1 s, for the model Participants = {p1, p2, p3}, MaxCrashes = 0, MaxParticipantCrashes = 0; the inductive step: TLC 2.19 explored 736 distinct states to depth 1 in 1 s, for the model Participants = {p1, p2, p3}, MaxCrashes = 0, MaxParticipantCrashes = 0; crashes: TLC 2.19 explored 3,448 distinct states to depth 12 in 3 s, for the model Participants = {p1, p2, p3}, MaxCrashes = 2, MaxParticipantCrashes = 0; the inductive step with crashes: TLC 2.19 explored 2,728 distinct states to depth 1 in 1 s, for the model Participants = {p1, p2, p3}, MaxCrashes = 1, MaxParticipantCrashes = 0; participant crashes: TLC 2.19 explored 12,754 distinct states to depth 12 in 10 s, for the model Participants = {p1, p2, p3}, MaxCrashes = 1, MaxParticipantCrashes = 1; the inductive step with participant crashes: TLC 2.19 explored 18,636 distinct states to depth 1 in 1 s, for the model Participants = {p1, p2, p3}, MaxCrashes = 1, MaxParticipantCrashes = 1; the recorded runs: TLC 2.19 explored 22 distinct states to depth 2 in 0 s, for the model Participants = {"p1", "p2", "p3"}, MaxCrashes = 2, MaxParticipantCrashes = 2.

This result was recorded before runs fingerprinted their inputs, so whether it still matches the current patch and sources is not known.

**Provenance:** Constructed as the second example of participant crashes in the two-phase-commit model, to pair with 093 and 095: the participant's counterpart of example 090, a change to the glue that no contract and no configuration of the model can see, caught by the recorded runs at the step where the log and the network disagree.

- [Cirstea, Kuppe, Loillier and Merz, Validating Traces of Distributed Programs Against TLA+ Specifications (2024): the technique, and what it finds that model checking the specification alone does not](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16075)
- [Gray, Notes on Data Base Operating Systems (1978): two-phase commit, the participants' and the coordinator's logs, and the write-ahead rule, log before act](https://jimgray.azurewebsites.net/papers/dbos.pdf)
- [Bernstein, Hadzilacos and Goodman, Concurrency Control and Recovery in Database Systems (1987), chapter 7: the participant's recovery procedure in two-phase commit, and the blocking property](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/people/philbe/book/)
- [TLC's action properties ([][A]_v in PROPERTIES): a property of every step, reported with the run up to the offending step](https://lamport.azurewebsites.net/tla/current-tools.pdf)
## Reproduce

```bash
python3 examples/tools/build.py 094
```

This applies `change.patch` to a temporary copy of the repo, runs the verifier on it, and rewrites this page.
